summary: Even with a median household income north of $230,000, Kentfield's median home value exceeding $2 million puts the price-to-income ratio above 8.6 — a figure that makes straightforward buying arithmetic difficult even at the top of the local income distribution. This unincorporated community of about 7,100, tucked into the eastern slopes of Mount Tamalpais in central Marin County, covers just three square miles of oak-studded hills and creekside flats where Ross Valley narrows toward Sir Francis Drake Boulevard, the main arterial funneling commuters toward the Richmond–San Rafael Bridge and, eventually, San Francisco. The area functions almost entirely as a bedroom community; the College of Marin campus is the most significant local employer, lending a faint academic rhythm without quite producing a college-town energy, while most working residents commute out. Average daily highs hover around 66°F year-round with nearly nine hours of sunshine, meaning the mild, dry summers and cool but rarely freezing winters reward the abundant trail access into open-space preserves climbing toward Tamalpais's ridgeline. Median rent near $2,500 is steep in absolute terms but strikingly modest relative to purchase prices, creating a place where the gap between owning and renting represents two almost entirely different financial realities.
